constraints.subject: openlobby.core.search.*
constraints.justification: ADR-0002: 'We will use Elasticsearch. It's well known database with great fulltext search capabilities based on Apache Lucene.' The 'database for all data' clause is content-superseded by ADR-0011: 'Elasticsearch will be used for denormalized reports and related data intended for fulltext search.' Post-resolution, ADR-0002's live mandate is Elasticsearch for fulltext search, whose locus is the search code (#125: post-resolution gold reading).

note: Product-scope ADR: 'frontend' and 'api_endpoint' are concepts, not checkable FQNs. No single-ADR-derivable, operationally-checkable constraint.

constraints.subject: openlobby.core.models.*
constraints.justification: ADR-0010 mandates Django as the web framework; relational data access goes through the Django ORM (django.db). Moved from ADR-0011 since the Django ORM choice is what makes django.db the access path.

note: Dropped in #125 (non-FQN-checkable, ADR-0003/0005 precedent): 'We will switch to Django.' is a framework choice with no FQN-derivable requires subject — settings.py is compliant Django-project code without importing django, so an import-level requires on openlobby.* asserts compliant modules are violating. The checkable content is carried by the flask prohibition and the models-locus django.db requires.
